postTitle: Don't Recompute Everything: Master useMemo in 60 Seconds
postContent:
Hook: Don’t recompute everything. useMemo caches the result of expensive calculations between renders. If inputs don’t change, React will reuse the previous value.

Plain terms: You give React a function and a list of dependencies. If any dependency changes, React recomputes. If not, it reuses the cached result.

Why it helps: It’s a small optimization that can prevent costly work when rendering large lists or heavy calculations.

When to use: UseMemo makes sense for expensive calculations or when you pass derived values to child components that rely on referential stability.

tehnicalChallange.title: Challenge: Measure the impact of useMemo
tehnicalChallange.description: Create a component rendering a large list and applying an expensive filter. Build two versions: one using useMemo for the derived data and one without. Compare render counts and timing. Practice choosing the right dependencies to avoid stale or unnecessary recomputations.
